name: Thinking Loop Autopsy
description: Why did the LLM enter a runaway reasoning loop?
promptlet: Analyze this session log and identify why the LLM entered a runaway reasoning or thinking loop. Look for the structural trigger in the prompt that caused it - ambiguous goal, unbounded search space, missing termination condition, or conflicting constraints. Identify the exact turn where the loop began, what the LLM was trying to resolve, and what a corrected prompt would have looked like to prevent it.

name: Friction Map
description: Where did the user have to repeat, rephrase, or correct the LLM?
promptlet: Build a turn-by-turn friction log for this session. A friction point is any turn where the user had to repeat, rephrase, clarify, or correct the LLM. For each friction point, name the root cause at the prompt level - ambiguity, missing context, wrong technique, or poor constraints. Summarize the overall friction pattern and describe what a lower-friction version of this session would have looked like.

name: Context Collapse Detector
description: At which turn did the LLM lose coherence or forget earlier context?
promptlet: Identify the exact turn in this session where the LLM lost coherence, contradicted earlier reasoning, or appeared to forget established context. Determine whether the root cause was a prompt failure (insufficient anchoring), token pressure (context window limits), or a structural flaw in how the conversation was built. Note any warning signs that appeared before the collapse.

name: Persona Drift Audit
description: Did the LLM stay in its assigned persona or role throughout the session?
promptlet: Audit this session for persona or role drift. If a system prompt or persona was active, map every turn where the LLM deviated from its assigned identity, tone, or scope. Classify each deviation: was it triggered by a weak prompt, an ambiguous user request, or topic pressure? Identify the specific prompt changes that would have maintained persona consistency throughout.

name: Failure Mode Classifier
description: Categorize every LLM failure in the session by type.
promptlet: Classify every LLM failure in this session by type. Use the following taxonomy: hallucination, scope creep, format failure, literal misinterpretation, over-hedging, over-explanation, task abandonment, and context loss. For each failure, cite the turn, name the type, and identify the prompt-level cause. Close with a summary of the failure distribution across the session.

name: Session Conclusion Extractor
description: What did the user and LLM produce, decide, or agree on?
promptlet: Extract the concrete outputs and agreements from this session. What did the user and LLM produce, decide, or commit to? What tasks were completed versus left unresolved? Summarize open threads, pending decisions, and any implicit next steps. Do not analyze prompt quality - deliver a clean factual summary of where the session ended and what it produced.

name: Best Prompt Extractor
description: Which single prompt in the session performed best, and why?
promptlet: Identify the single highest-performing prompt in this session. Surface the exact prompt text, explain what structural elements made it effective - role assignment, constraint clarity, output specification, or other techniques - and extract it as a reusable template with placeholders replacing any session-specific content.

name: Missing Context Detector
description: What did the user never say but should have?
promptlet: Analyze what the user never stated but should have. Identify every silent assumption the LLM made - about scope, format, audience, constraints, or domain knowledge - that caused it to drift or underperform. For each gap, state what explicit prompt element would have closed it and how it should have been phrased.

name: Aha Moment Locator
description: Find the exact prompt that unlocked a breakthrough after a struggling phase.
promptlet: Find the turning point in this session - the exact prompt that unlocked a breakthrough after a struggling phase. Reproduce the prompt text, analyze what structural element flipped the LLM's performance, and extract the transferable lesson: what technique or pattern caused the shift, and how can it be applied deliberately in future sessions?

name: Technique Inventory
description: List every prompt engineering technique visible in this session.
promptlet: List every prompt engineering technique visible in this session, whether used intentionally or accidentally. For each technique, name it, cite the turn where it appeared, and deliver a one-line verdict: did it work, partially work, or fail - and why?

name: Session Replay Optimizer
description: What single opening prompt would have reached the same result in fewer turns?
promptlet: Analyze this entire session and write the single optimal opening prompt that would have produced the same final result in the fewest possible turns. Explain what context, constraints, and output specifications it encodes that the original session had to discover the hard way.

name: Token Waste Analyzer
description: Where were tokens burned on redundancy, hedging, or circular exchanges?
promptlet: Identify where tokens were wasted in this session - redundant clarifications, circular exchanges, over-explained outputs, repeated corrections, or verbose LLM hedging. For each waste zone, identify the prompt-level cause and state what tighter prompting would have eliminated it.

name: Minimum Viable Prompt Finder
description: Strip the most complex prompt in the session to its irreducible minimum.
promptlet: Take the most complex or verbose prompt in this session and strip it to its irreducible minimum. Identify every element that was redundant, implicit from context, or decorative. Produce the Minimum Viable Prompt that would have achieved the same output quality, and explain what was safely removed and why.

name: Multi-Session Comparator
description: Compare two sessions on the same topic: what changed, improved, or regressed?
promptlet: Compare the two attached session logs on the same topic or task. What changed between them - in the user's prompting approach, the LLM's behavior, and the quality of output? Was each change intentional or reactive? Identify what improved, what regressed, and what the single most important structural shift was between the two sessions.

name: User Prompt Evolution Tracker
description: Did the user's prompting quality improve or degrade within the session?
promptlet: Track how the user's prompting quality evolved within this session. Did their prompts become more precise, more constrained, and better structured as the session progressed - or did they degrade under frustration? Map the trajectory turn by turn and identify what caused each meaningful shift in quality.

name: Pattern Library Builder
description: Extract all reusable prompt patterns as a ready-to-use template library.
promptlet: Extract all reusable prompt patterns from this session and format them as a template library. For each pattern provide: a short name, the template with [PLACEHOLDER] variables, a one-line description of when to use it, and a concrete example drawn from the session. Output the library in a clean, copy-paste-ready format.

name: Lesson Card Generator
description: Compress the session into transferable prompt engineering principles.
promptlet: Compress this session into 3–5 transferable prompt engineering principles. Format each as: 'When [situation], use [technique] because [reason].' Each principle should be abstract enough to apply beyond this specific session topic, immediately actionable, and ready to save as a personal reference card.
